object_context: Determine whether nonempty pair intersections provide essential source-native power for full Cavalar-Oliveira semi-filter cover complexity beyond all-disjoint pair covers, before introducing any higher-order closure/fusion-depth invariant.
problem_signature: pair preservation E,H in F => E intersection H in F
representation invariance across equivalent optimal cover witnesses
canonical first-order signature lane already logarithmically capped
structural_coordinates: C008 proves rho_can=1<rho=2 on one 3x3 graph, so noncanonical semi-filters contain information absent from canonical witnesses
C010 gives an optimal two-pair disjoint generator-separating cover for that same C008 graph, so C008 does not show that nonempty intersections or ancestry of a chosen cover program are essential
C024 shows a source-native one-pair fractional budget but loses integral cross-pair correlation
C025 restores integral joint consistency on normalized G_NEQ but returns to a canonical first-order signature class with logarithmic capacity
C016 shows fixed finite-state aggregation with fixed local symbol cost yields O(log N) full cover complexity even for dense globally correlated families
the next representation must be defined from source obligations or equivalence classes of valid covers, not from arbitrary syntax of one witness
any finite calibration must distinguish unrestricted full-cover power from disjoint-pair cover power before asymptotic lower-bound search
equivalent_formulations: compare unrestricted full cover number rho with the minimum cover number rho_disj obtained when every selected pair (E,H) satisfies E intersection H=emptyset
ask whether every optimal full-cover family can be replaced, without increasing cardinality, by an all-disjoint family
search for a finite graph whose full-cover optimum strictly improves when non-disjoint pairs are allowed
treat absence of a small gap as route-pruning evidence, not a theorem that no gap exists asymptotically

C025 exact normalized G_NEQ joint-signature calibration
near_solved_analogues: restricted-family set cover: compare optimum over all covering sets with optimum over a structurally restricted admissible subfamily
fractional-cover versus integral-cover gaps in communication complexity

method_transfers.method: test representation invariance by comparing the unrestricted optimum with an optimum restricted to all-disjoint pair witnesses
shared_structure: both optimize finite pair families against exactly the same full semi-filter obligation universe
disjoint pairs are source-valid and immediately refute preservation whenever both sides belong to a semi-filter
a strict optimum gap would certify that nonempty intersections are operationally useful rather than an artifact of one chosen proof
required_assumptions: the restricted optimum is computed against the exact source Definition 20 preservation predicate
the same graph and full relevant semi-filter universe are used in both optima
disanalogies: rho_disj>rho would establish essential non-disjoint pair power only for that finite object, not an asymptotic lower bound
rho_disj=rho on small objects would not prove global eliminability of non-disjoint pairs
method_transfers.repair_question: Is there any small full-cover instance on which non-disjoint pairs strictly reduce the exact cover cardinality?

method_transfers.method: use a known calibration failure and its repair to require that any new coordinate recover missing correlation without collapsing back into a previously capped representation class
shared_structure: both concern the same cover graph and simultaneous choice of pair vertices
local validity is insufficient if global compatibility or capacity collapses

explicit_disanalogies: noncanonical full-cover difficulty is not the same as essential nonempty-intersection difficulty
the existence of one non-disjoint optimal witness does not imply every optimum needs non-disjoint pairs
a finite restricted-vs-unrestricted optimum gap is not an asymptotic circuit lower bound
no small gap is not a global no-go theorem
generic set-cover hierarchy results do not establish semi-filter-cover hierarchy behavior

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: Two programs can compute the same function while using different intermediate variables; a property of one program's temporary variable is not a property of the function unless it is invariant across equivalent implementations.
common_abstraction: target authority belongs to an object-level behavior rather than one witness syntax
multiple witnesses can realize the same optimum
intermediate structure is useful only if it survives or is forced across equivalent witnesses
source_to_target_mapping: program output behavior -> covering the same full semi-filter universe
temporary variable/intermediate -> nonempty intersection or derived closure element in one cover witness
implementation-invariant property -> strict advantage over every all-disjoint optimal witness
shared_constraints: same target obligations and same objective cardinality must be held fixed
disanalogies: cover pairs are mathematical sets under a source preservation law, not executable instructions
a strict disjoint-cover gap certifies necessity of non-disjoint pair power only at the finite instance and cardinality objective
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Before promoting closure-depth or ancestry as a state coordinate, prove that the target behavior cannot be achieved equally well by a representation that removes that intermediate structure.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: Freeze an exact restricted-vs-unrestricted cover oracle and search a bounded graph universe for rho_disj>rho; record nulls and exact search boundary.
